capability: Deterministic hash-chained run-archive integrity foundation. RunArchive::create(base, run_id, manifest) creates a per-run directory with manifest.json + empty events.jsonl. RunArchive::append(event_type, candidate_id, generation, payload) appends one line-delimited JSON event with event_hash = stable_hash({schema, sequence, run_id, event_type, candidate_id, generation, payload, previous_event_hash}) (Haber-Stornetta 1991 hash-chain linking). RunArchive::final_state(state) writes final-state.json plus provenance.json binding manifest_sha256 + events_sha256 + event_chain_root + final_state_hash with a root_hash = stable_hash({run_id, manifest_sha256, events_sha256, event_chain_root, final_state_hash}). verify_run(path) independently recomputes every hash and asserts (a) contiguous sequence 1..N, (b) all four component hashes match the provenance record, (c) observed root_hash == stable_hash(expected). Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, regulatory, safety, or product-performance authority; signature_status is pinned to UNSIGNED_CONTROLLED_KEY_REQUIRED and promotion_receipt_eligible is pinned to false until the controlled-key signing pipeline is authorized.
population: Three positive archive scenarios (empty=0 events, small=3 events, complex=12 events across 3 generations) plus 10 dedicated tamper probes each mutating exactly one integrity condition: tampered manifest bytes; appended extra line to events.jsonl; tampered final-state.json; tampered provenance.json root_hash; tampered provenance.json events_sha256; sequence gap in events; mutated event payload without updating event_hash; missing provenance.json; missing manifest.json; duplicate RunArchive::create against same base+run_id.
split_methodology: No fitting - hash-chained run provenance is closed-form SHA-256 arithmetic + append-only event log + strict independent recompute. The harness builds real archives under tempdir using the public RunArchive API, then invokes verify_run and asserts the returned root_hash equals an independently-recomputed stable_hash of the same 5 expected fields. Every tamper probe mutates one field/file/byte and asserts verify_run returns Err with the correct RunArchiveError variant. Byte-stability of the KPI receipt across replays is achieved by recording only the error variant name (Exists/Integrity/Io/Json/Contract) instead of the tempdir-dependent error string, so successive runs on different tempdirs produce byte-identical result.v1.json.
theory: Haber and Stornetta 1991 'How to time-stamp a digital document' Journal of Cryptology 3(2):99-111 - foundational hash-chain time-stamping methodology that the append() previous_event_hash → event_hash link implements. Merkle 1980 'Protocols for public key cryptosystems' IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy - Merkle tree/chain construction. RFC 6962 (2013) 'Certificate Transparency' - append-only tamper-evident log methodology adopted by Certificate Transparency. Torvalds and Hamano 2005 git (SHA-1 commit tree) - hash-based content-addressable object store; the RunArchive event chain is a per-run linear analog. in-toto Attestation Framework v1.0 (2020) - subject/predicate signed-artifact binding methodology. SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) v1.0 (2023) - reproducible provenance requirements. NIST FIPS 180-4 (2015) 'Secure Hash Standard' - SHA-256 specification. NIST SP 800-92 (2006) 'Guide to Computer Security Log Management' - append-only log integrity requirements. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A.12.4 (Logging and monitoring) + A.8.15 (Logging) - audit-log integrity controls. Anderson 1980 'Computer Security Threat Monitoring and Surveillance' - foundational reference-monitor + audit-log threat model. Salzer and Schroeder 1975 Proceedings of the IEEE 63(9):1278-1308 - complete-mediation methodology.

metrics.name: integrity_tamper_probes_fail_closed_rate
metrics.note: For 10/10 tamper probes, verify_run (or RunArchive::create for the duplicate-create probe) returns the expected RunArchiveError variant. Coverage: manifest bytes mutation → Integrity; events.jsonl mutation → Integrity (or Json/Contract if malformed); final-state.json mutation → Integrity; provenance root_hash tampering → Integrity; provenance events_sha256 tampering → Integrity; sequence gap → Integrity (non-contiguous); mutated event payload → Integrity (chain root mismatch); missing provenance.json → Io; missing manifest.json → Io; duplicate archive create → Exists.

fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.prediction_rule: For RunArchive::create(base, run_id, manifest): (1) verify base/run_id does not already exist (else Exists); (2) create directory + write manifest.json + open empty events.jsonl. For RunArchive::append(event_type, candidate_id, generation, payload): (3) increment sequence; (4) compute event_hash = stable_hash({schema, sequence, run_id, event_type, candidate_id, generation, payload, previous_event_hash}); (5) append line-delimited JSON. For RunArchive::final_state(state): (6) write final-state.json + provenance.json with manifest_sha256=SHA-256(manifest bytes), events_sha256=SHA-256(events bytes), event_chain_root=last event_hash (or SHA-256(empty)), final_state_hash=stable_hash(state), root_hash=stable_hash of the 5-field seed, signature_status='UNSIGNED_CONTROLLED_KEY_REQUIRED', promotion_receipt_eligible=false. For verify_run(path): (7) read provenance/manifest/events/final-state; (8) verify contiguous sequence 1..N (else Integrity); (9) verify manifest_sha256, events_sha256, event_chain_root, final_state_hash all match provenance; (10) verify observed root_hash == stable_hash(expected). Runtime is content-addressable end-to-end; any single-bit mutation of any artifact fails verify_run.
fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.hash_algorithm_root_hash: stable_hash of {run_id, manifest_sha256, events_sha256, event_chain_root, final_state_hash}
fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.note: Foundational hash-chained run archive.
